questions.prompt: A hard-IRQ handler and process context share a short invariant on one CPU. Which process-context primitive prevents self-deadlock from local interrupt re-entry?
options: A plain spin_lock with interrupts unchanged
questions.explanation: Saving and disabling local interrupts while taking the spinlock prevents that CPU's handler from interrupting the holder and taking the same lock.

questions.prompt: Why is a mutex invalid in hard-IRQ context?
options: Mutex acquisition may sleep, while hard-IRQ context cannot sleep
Mutexes provide no mutual exclusion on SMP
A mutex always disables all interrupts
questions.explanation: Contended mutex acquisition can block and schedule; hard-IRQ context is atomic and cannot sleep.

questions.prompt: Which fact must be established before choosing a synchronization primitive?
options: Whether every accessor can sleep and which contexts can interrupt each other
questions.explanation: Context, sleepability, concurrency, critical-section length, and lifetime determine legal primitive choices.

questions.prompt: What does disabling preemption alone fail to prevent?
options: A local hard interrupt accessing the same state
questions.explanation: Preemption control keeps task context on a CPU but does not mask hard interrupts.

questions.prompt: In message passing, what does an acquire load that reads from a release store establish?
options: Prior writes sequenced before the release happen-before operations after the acquire
Every relaxed operation becomes sequentially consistent
questions.explanation: The synchronizes-with edge carries earlier published state to the acquiring reader.

questions.prompt: Why is atomicity alone insufficient for publishing related data?
options: Atomic operations cannot be used by threads
An atomic flag can be indivisible without ordering surrounding data accesses
Atomic values are always wider than cache lines
questions.explanation: Atomicity protects the flag operation itself; ordering is required to publish the associated state.

questions.prompt: Which Linux primitive expresses a write-side publication edge paired with smp_load_acquire()?
questions.explanation: The release store and acquire load form the intended inter-CPU publication relationship when the value is observed.

questions.prompt: What does compiler barrier() guarantee by itself?
options: A full hardware memory fence on every architecture
No relevant compiler reordering across the barrier, but no standalone hardware-order guarantee
questions.explanation: A compiler barrier constrains compilation; architecture memory barriers are separate.

questions.prompt: Why must spinlock critical sections be bounded and non-sleeping?
options: The holder executes with no C stack
A sleeper can retain the lock while waiters burn CPU and may deadlock
Spinlocks work only for one instruction
questions.explanation: Spin waiters make progress only when the holder runs and releases; sleeping while holding violates that progress model.

questions.prompt: What does spin_lock_irqsave(lock, flags) preserve that spin_lock_irq(lock) does not?
options: The local CPU's prior interrupt-enable state for restoration
The global interrupt state of every CPU
questions.explanation: irqsave records local flags so unlock_irqrestore restores the entry state rather than unconditionally enabling interrupts.

questions.prompt: Two paths acquire A then B and B then A. What is the primary risk?
questions.explanation: Opposite nested order can leave each holder waiting forever for the other's lock.

questions.prompt: Does a spinlock on CPU 0 disable interrupts on CPU 1?
options: No; local IRQ masking is local, while lock ownership serializes CPUs
Only if the lock is contended
questions.explanation: Local interrupt control affects one CPU; the shared lock provides cross-CPU exclusion.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a Linux mutex from a raw spinlock under contention?
options: The mutex may sleep; the raw spinlock waiter spins
questions.explanation: Mutexes are sleeping locks for sleepable context, whereas raw spinlocks preserve atomic-context semantics.

questions.prompt: What problem does priority inheritance address?
options: Unbounded inversion caused when a low-priority owner blocks a higher-priority waiter
questions.explanation: PI temporarily boosts the owner so it can run and release the contended lock sooner.

questions.prompt: What does successful pthread_mutexattr_setprotocol(PTHREAD_PRIO_INHERIT) prove in this lab?
options: The platform accepted creation of a PI-protocol mutex attribute
Linux rtmutex internals executed exactly once
questions.explanation: The observation is API support only; the lab requests no RT policy and establishes no latency guarantee.

questions.prompt: Why must a condition protected by a mutex be checked in a loop?
options: Wakeups can be spurious or another waiter can consume the condition
questions.explanation: The predicate, not the wakeup itself, authorizes progress after mutex reacquisition.

questions.prompt: What does refcount_inc_not_zero-style acquisition prevent?
options: Taking a reference after the object has reached its terminal zero state
questions.explanation: Conditional increment avoids resurrecting an object whose final reference has already been dropped.

questions.prompt: Why does a seqlock reader retry when the sequence changed or is odd?
options: The writer may have been active or modified the snapshot during the read
The reader must become the writer
questions.explanation: An odd or changed sequence means the fields may not form one stable version.

questions.prompt: What is a key seqlock suitability constraint?
options: Readers may safely retain arbitrary pointers after retry validation
Writers must be serialized, and copied reader data must tolerate retry
Readers may sleep forever inside a kernel read section
questions.explanation: Writers require serialization; readers optimistically copy and retry rather than holding unstable pointer lifetimes.

questions.prompt: Why can per-CPU counters scale better than one global counter?
options: They eliminate all synchronization in every operation
They localize frequent updates and aggregate less frequently, reducing cache-line contention
They are always exact without aggregation
questions.explanation: Per-CPU state trades immediate global aggregation for locality and less shared-line bouncing.

days.title: RCU Readers, Grace Periods, and Callbacks

questions.prompt: What may an RCU reader assume about an object reached through a protected pointer?
options: It can sleep indefinitely in every RCU flavor
The object will not be reclaimed before the relevant read-side critical section ends
No updater can publish a replacement
The object's fields are automatically immutable
questions.explanation: RCU protects lifetime through the read-side section; separate synchronization governs mutation and publication.

questions.prompt: What does an RCU grace period wait for?
options: All pre-existing relevant readers to pass through a quiescent state or finish
questions.explanation: Grace periods are reader-progress conditions, not fixed timers.

questions.prompt: Why does call_rcu defer reclamation?
options: To execute the callback before publication
To run the callback after a grace period so old readers cannot still hold the removed object
To turn a mutex into a spinlock
To make readers increment a shared refcount
questions.explanation: Removal and reclamation are separated so readers that saw the old pointer can finish.

questions.prompt: What does the userspace epoch lab establish?
options: A bounded model can publish a new version, wait for registered old-epoch readers, then reclaim
questions.explanation: The program teaches the lifetime sequence only and is explicitly not a Linux RCU implementation.

days.title: Lockdep, KCSAN, RCU Stalls, and Debug Reports

questions.prompt: What does lockdep primarily reason about?
options: Observed lock-class acquisition dependencies and context rules
C language undefined behavior in userspace
questions.explanation: Lockdep tracks dependency relationships and lock usage to report potential deadlocks and misuse.

questions.prompt: What kind of defect is KCSAN designed to detect?
options: Potential data races through sampled watchpoints and concurrency instrumentation
questions.explanation: KCSAN dynamically samples conflicting accesses to identify race candidates; absence of a report is not proof of race freedom.

questions.prompt: An RCU stall warning proves which narrow fact?
options: A diagnostic threshold observed insufficient grace-period/read-side progress
The exact guilty source line is known
questions.explanation: A stall warning is evidence of delayed progress and context; root cause still requires correlated evidence.

questions.prompt: A privileged tracing tool is unavailable. What should the report say?
options: Infer the expected trace from source
SKIP with the concrete reason and keep event-level claims unknown
questions.explanation: Honest SKIP preserves the boundary between source knowledge, available observations, and unobserved events.
